text:
Marta: quick heads-up — noticed the realtime quota scrub heuristic bumped sampling to 100% during the EU burst window this morning. that exposed unredacted request snippets in the ephemeral inspector.
Raj: whoa, 100%? that shouldn't happen — scrub heuristics should cap at 20% for chatty routes. any idea which rollout change triggered it?
Marta: looks tied to the new quota-autotune flag we flipped for canary — it tried to keep latency under 40ms by disabling KV-prefetch cutoff, and samplerPolicy fell back to `full_capture` for a subset of routes.
Zach: ugh. that fallback path was supposed to be gated by consent-tier checks. maybe route metadata wasn't propagated to the sampler service.
Leo: I dug into the trace. the sampler call from gateway lacked `route.consent_level` in headers during the burst. gateway PR 4821 added async metadata batching; the edge case is when metadata queue is full we send minimal headers.
Jena: minimal headers are fine for throughput, but sampler needs consent for PII redaction decisions. We should make consent propagation synchronous before sampler call or add a safe default that redacts when unknown.
Raj: +1 to safe default. otherwise we break the principle of least privilege. can we patch sampler to treat missing consent as `sensitive` until header arrives?
Marta: we can ship a hotfix to sampler to treat missing as sensitive, but that won't fix historical captures. need quick mitigation on console/inspector UI to hide raw snippets when flagged from canary.
Infra-bot: deploy started: sampler-service v3.4.7-hotfix to canary (hosts: svc-sampler-01,02)
Zach: also recommend adding a `scrub-mode` toggle in the console rollout UI so operators can flip to aggressive-scrub across all routes during incidents. Right now rollback is binary and slow.
Leo: Agreed. UX should let SREs quickly set sampling-mode=`,aggressive_scrub` for tenant or route. We can wire it to the smart-routing policy so it respects quotas.
Jena: Two action items: 1) patch sampler to default to sensitive on missing consent (hotfix). 2) console UX toggle + metric that counts "missing-consent headers -> full_capture fallback".
Raj: add telemetry for "sampler_fallback_reason" with labels: route, tenant, upstream_version. we need dashboards and an alert when fallback_rate > 1% for any tenant.
Marta: I'll open a small dashboard: realtime -> panels: fallback_rate, scrubbed_snippets_count, average_kv_latency. We should also add a historical scrub audit for last 24h for the affected canary tenants.
Zach: For rollout policy: change autotune so it does not flip samplerPolicy to `full_capture` unless both KV latency < 20ms AND consent present. otherwise it should lower requests-per-second instead of changing scrub behavior.
Leo: I'll revert the async metadata batching change for the canary traffic as immediate mitigation — it will lower throughput a bit but keep telemetry safe.
Jena: Are we worried about cost if we keep aggressive_scrub on too long? we should have an automatic decay that returns to prior mode after 10m unless manually extended.
Marta: makes sense. auto-decay + an audit note required when extended past 10m. we'll log operator identity.
Raj: Proposal: alert playbook -> PagerDuty escalation if fallback_rate > 5% for 5m, otherwise slack alert to #eng-platform at 1% for 10m. Also annotate alert with sample traces (redacted) and affected tenants.
Zach: i'll draft the playbook and update the runbooks repo. also a PR to add consent propagation unit tests.
Infra-bot: deploy success: sampler-service v3.4.7-hotfix canary complete at 1758901250
Marta: thanks. i'll follow up with a postmortem-lite in #postmortems and attach the dashboard. quick note to everyone: treat missing consent as a severity-3 privacy incident until we harden the path. :exclamation:
Leo: 👍
Jena: thanks all — will create RFC for the UX toggle and autopatch timeline.
